chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Gigging with Sy Oliver's band
summary: He did club dates with Oliver's band, including a two-week Jersey nightclub show, while Kirby had no work.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, now, at this time you were also playing with Sy Oliver.
I'm all through with Sy. Didn't I... I gave you about Sy, didn't I?
Well, I took it down, but we didn't do it on the tape.
Well, I mean, there's not much to say about Sy. Except I guess you got the reed section, except I can't think of the brass section.
But while you were in and out with Kirby, you were also gigging with Sy, right?

Well, I'd gig with anybody. See, I went out with Kirby, because he wasn't doin' nothin'. And in fact, wasn't anybody doin' anything. As it come, that's what you did. Just like the boys are doing today. They're still doing it.
What kind of jobs did Sy have, then? Mostly dances?

What kind of jobs did he have? Yeah, all of them were dances, except that one we had over in Jersey. That was a two-week thing in a nightclub. That was a big show. The rest of them were just dances, what you call club dates.
And the band that he had at that time was George Dorsey, first alto; Dave McRae, baritone, and he was the straw boss, you said, the guy who hired the musicians...
Joe Garland on tenor. Charlie Rouse on tenor?
Al McCrumble(?) on trombone. Sy Oliver on trumpet. Freddie Green on guitar. Plus other musicians that you don't remember. Well, from this point on, then, you were really just gigging.
